items.name: Introduction to Cybersecurity
items.description: The most recommended first course: a short, self-paced tour of threats, defences and careers, with no prerequisites.

items.name: Pre Security path
items.description: Networking, the web, Linux and Windows basics, taught through guided rooms in your browser.

items.name: CS50’s Introduction to Cybersecurity
items.description: Harvard’s lecture series on securing accounts, data, systems and software. Clear, rigorous and free.

items.name: Bandit
items.description: Learn the Linux command line by solving levels in a real shell over SSH. The classic first wargame.

items.name: Cyber Security roadmap
items.description: A community-maintained map of what to learn, in what order, with links for every topic.

items.name: Security+ training course
items.description: A complete, free video course for CompTIA Security+, plus Network+ and A+. Great foundations even if you never sit the exam.

items.name: Google Cybersecurity Certificate
items.description: Eight courses covering security basics, networks, Linux, SQL, Python and SIEM tools. Course material can usually be audited; the certificate needs a subscription.

items.name: Cybersecurity learning plans
items.description: Free self-paced cybersecurity fundamentals with IBM digital badges on completion.

items.name: Linux Journey
items.description: Bite-sized Linux lessons, from the command line to processes, permissions and networking.

items.name: CS50x
items.description: The best-known introduction to programming. Knowing how software is built makes you far better at securing it.

items.name: Security, Compliance and Identity Fundamentals
items.description: Free learning path for SC-900: identity, Zero Trust and Microsoft’s security tooling.

items.name: Free Splunk training
items.description: Learn to search logs and build dashboards in one of the SIEMs SOC teams use most.

items.name: Fortinet Training Institute
items.description: Free self-paced security awareness and fundamentals courses, with certificates of completion.

items.name: OpenSecurityTraining2
items.description: Deep, free classes on x86-64 assembly, reverse engineering, firmware and vulnerability research.

items.name: Reverse engineering workshops
items.description: Hands-on RE101 and RE102 workshops that walk you through taking real malware apart.

items.name: Computer Systems Security (6.858)
items.description: MIT’s full university course: lectures, papers and labs on how systems are attacked and defended.

items.name: Cybrary
items.description: Video courses across IT and security. A good chunk is free; career paths and labs are paid.

items.name: TCM Security Academy
items.description: Practical, affordable courses on ethical hacking, SOC work and OSINT. Several courses are free.

items.name: Antisyphon Training
items.description: Live, practitioner-led classes from the Black Hills Information Security crowd, many offered pay-what-you-can.

items.name: SANS courses
items.description: The industry’s most in-depth (and expensive) training. Often employer-funded; worth it for specialists.

items.name: TryHackMe
items.description: Guided, browser-based rooms for every skill level, with paths for SOC analysts, pentesters and more.

items.name: Hack The Box
items.description: Vulnerable machines and challenges to hack, from easy to insane, plus the structured HTB Academy.

items.name: picoCTF
items.description: Beginner-friendly capture-the-flag challenges with a year-round practice gym.

items.name: Web Security Academy
items.description: Free interactive labs for every major web vulnerability, written by the makers of Burp Suite.

items.name: CyberDefenders
items.description: Blue-team labs built on real forensic artefacts, packet captures and logs.

items.name: Blue Team Labs Online
items.description: Defensive investigations and challenges in incident response, log analysis and forensics.

items.name: LetsDefend
items.description: A simulated SOC: work alerts in a SIEM, investigate, and close cases like a Tier 1 analyst.

items.name: pwn.college
items.description: A free, belt-based dojo for binary exploitation, Linux internals and system security.

items.name: OverTheWire wargames
items.description: After Bandit: Natas for web, Leviathan, Narnia and more for exploitation.

items.name: Root Me
items.description: Hundreds of challenges across web, crypto, forensics, networking and reversing.

items.name: Hacker101
items.description: Free web-security video lessons and a CTF, aimed at would-be bug bounty hunters.

items.name: OWASP Juice Shop
items.description: A deliberately insecure web shop you run locally, packed with the OWASP Top 10 and more.

items.name: VulnHub
items.description: Download vulnerable virtual machines to hack offline in your own lab.

items.name: Cryptopals
items.description: Break real cryptography by implementing attacks yourself, one challenge set at a time.

items.name: crackmes.one
items.description: Small programs made to be reverse engineered, rated by difficulty.

items.name: Boss of the SOC v3 dataset
items.description: A full, realistic attack dataset to load into Splunk and investigate at your own pace.

items.name: PentesterLab
items.description: Focused web-hacking exercises that build from basics to code review. Some exercises are free.

items.name: CTFtime
items.description: The calendar of upcoming capture-the-flag competitions, plus write-ups of past ones.

items.name: CompTIA Security+
items.description: The most common entry-level security certification, often required for government roles. Prepare free with Professor Messer.

items.name: Certified in Cybersecurity (CC)
items.description: An entry-level certification from ISC2. Its free exam programme closed to new sign-ups in May 2026.

items.name: CompTIA CySA+
items.description: The step after Security+ for analysts: threat detection, log analysis and incident response.

items.name: Security Operations Analyst (SC-200)
items.description: Defender and Sentinel skills for SOC work. The training is free on Microsoft Learn; the exam is paid.

items.name: Blue Team Level 1 (BTL1)
items.description: A practical, exam-in-a-lab defensive certification well regarded for junior SOC roles.

items.name: eJPT
items.description: A hands-on, entry-level penetration testing exam. A common first offensive cert.

items.name: PNPT
items.description: A five-day practical pentest exam that ends with writing and presenting a real report.

items.name: HTB Certified Penetration Testing Specialist
items.description: A demanding, report-based pentest exam backed by HTB Academy’s penetration tester path.

items.name: OSCP (PEN-200)
items.description: The best-known hands-on pentesting certification, with a 24-hour practical exam.

items.name: GIAC Certified Incident Handler (GCIH)
items.description: A respected incident-response certification, usually paired with SANS SEC504.

items.name: GIAC Certified Forensic Analyst (GCFA)
items.description: Advanced incident response and threat-hunting forensics across Windows and memory.

items.name: CISSP
items.description: The senior, management-leaning certification. Requires around five years of experience.

items.name: Security Certification Roadmap
items.description: Hundreds of certifications on one chart, grouped by domain and level. Useful for spotting where a cert fits.

items.name: CyberChef
items.description: Encode, decode, decrypt and analyse data in your browser. The “Cyber Swiss Army Knife”.

items.name: Wireshark
items.description: The go-to network protocol analyser for capturing and inspecting traffic.

items.name: Nmap
items.description: The standard network scanner for finding hosts, open ports and services. The free Nmap book is online too.

items.name: Burp Suite Community Edition
items.description: Intercept and modify web traffic. Essential for web application testing.

items.name: Kali Linux
items.description: A Linux distribution with hundreds of security tools preinstalled.

items.name: Sysinternals Suite
items.description: Process Explorer, Autoruns, Sysmon and more: Windows utilities for troubleshooting and investigation.

items.name: Ghidra
items.description: An open-source reverse engineering framework with a decompiler.

items.name: Volatility
items.description: The open-source standard for memory forensics.

items.name: Autopsy
items.description: A graphical digital forensics platform for disk images and phones.

items.name: Eric Zimmerman’s tools
items.description: Parsers for Prefetch, the registry, event logs, LNK files and more, used across the DFIR world.

items.name: Velociraptor
items.description: Open-source endpoint visibility and collection for incident response and threat hunting.

items.name: Security Onion
items.description: A free Linux platform for threat hunting, network monitoring and log management. Ideal for a home lab.

items.name: Wazuh
items.description: An open-source SIEM and XDR you can run in a home lab to practise detection.

items.name: Zeek
items.description: Turns network traffic into rich, searchable logs for detection and investigation.

items.name: Suricata
items.description: A high-performance open-source intrusion detection and prevention engine.

items.name: REMnux
items.description: A Linux toolkit for reverse engineering and analysing malware.

items.name: FLARE-VM
items.description: Scripts that turn a Windows VM into a malware analysis workstation.

items.name: VirusTotal
items.description: Check files, hashes, URLs and domains against dozens of security engines.

items.name: ANY.RUN
items.description: An interactive online sandbox: detonate a sample and watch what it does.

items.name: urlscan.io
items.description: Safely scan a suspicious URL and see what the page loads and where it connects.

items.name: Shodan
items.description: A search engine for internet-connected devices. Great for OSINT and exposure research.

items.name: Hashcat
items.description: Fast, GPU-powered password recovery for testing password strength.

items.name: YARA
items.description: Write rules that describe and detect malware by its patterns.

items.name: Sigma
items.description: A generic detection-rule format that converts to most SIEMs, with thousands of community rules.

items.name: explainshell
items.description: Paste a command and see what every part of it does.

items.name: MITRE ATT&CK
items.description: The shared language for adversary tactics and techniques, used by every SOC.

items.name: MITRE D3FEND
items.description: ATT&CK’s defensive counterpart: a map of countermeasures and how they relate to attacks.

items.name: OWASP Top 10
items.description: The standard awareness document for the most critical web application risks.

items.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
items.description: A practical way to understand and organise a security programme: govern, identify, protect, detect, respond, recover.

items.name: CIS Critical Security Controls
items.description: A prioritised list of safeguards that stop the most common attacks.

items.name: Cyber Kill Chain
items.description: The seven-stage model of an intrusion that shaped how defenders think about attacks.

items.name: Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
items.description: Vulnerabilities attackers are actively exploiting right now. Patch these first.

items.name: LOLBAS
items.description: Windows binaries, scripts and libraries attackers abuse, and how to spot them.

items.name: GTFOBins
items.description: Unix binaries that can be used to bypass local security restrictions.

items.name: HackTricks
items.description: A huge, community-written wiki of pentesting techniques and tricks.

items.name: PayloadsAllTheThings
items.description: Payloads and bypasses for web application testing, organised by vulnerability.

items.name: Atomic Red Team
items.description: Small, safe tests mapped to ATT&CK so you can check whether your detections fire.

items.name: Windows Security Log Encyclopedia
items.description: What every Windows event ID means, with examples. Indispensable during investigations.

items.name: SANS posters & cheat sheets
items.description: Free reference posters on Windows forensics, hunting evil, memory analysis and more.

items.name: NIST Glossary
items.description: Authoritative definitions for thousands of security terms, with sources.

items.name: The Linux Command Line
items.description: A complete book on the Linux shell, free to read online.

items.name: Security Engineering
items.description: The classic on building dependable systems. Earlier editions are free to download.

items.name: Incident Response Recommendations (SP 800-61r3)
items.description: NIST’s guidance on incident response, tied to the Cybersecurity Framework 2.0.

items.name: Online Investigation Toolkit
items.description: The tools Bellingcat’s own investigators use, with how-to notes for each.

items.name: Beej’s Guide to Network Programming
items.description: A friendly, free guide to how sockets and networking really work.

items.name: A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography
items.description: A rigorous, free textbook on modern cryptography.

items.name: Linux Basics for Hackers
items.description: Linux taught through a security lens: networking, scripting and staying anonymous.

items.name: Practical Malware Analysis
items.description: Still the go-to hands-on introduction to taking malware apart.

items.name: The Practice of Network Security Monitoring
items.description: Richard Bejtlich on collecting and analysing network data to catch intruders.

items.name: Real-World Bug Hunting
items.description: Web vulnerabilities explained through real, paid bug bounty reports.

items.name: Serious Cryptography
items.description: A practical, readable guide to how modern encryption works and fails.

items.name: OSINT Techniques
items.description: The OSINT practitioner’s reference, updated with each edition.

items.name: John Hammond
items.description: CTF walkthroughs, malware analysis and news, explained with energy.

items.name: NetworkChuck
items.description: Approachable videos on networking, Linux and home labs for beginners.

items.name: IppSec
items.description: Detailed Hack The Box walkthroughs. Search them all at ippsec.rocks.

items.name: 13Cubed
items.description: Clear, deep dives into Windows, Linux and memory forensics.

items.name: LiveOverflow
items.description: How hacking really works, from binary exploitation to web bugs.

items.name: Simply Cyber
items.description: Gerald Auger on breaking into cybersecurity, plus a daily news brief.

items.name: Black Hills Information Security
items.description: Free webcasts from working pentesters and defenders.

items.name: SANS Digital Forensics and Incident Response
items.description: Conference talks and webcasts from the DFIR community.

items.name: Darknet Diaries
items.description: True stories from the dark side of the internet. The best way into the field for many listeners.

items.name: Risky Business
items.description: Weekly security news and analysis, a staple for practitioners.

items.name: SANS Internet Stormcast
items.description: A daily five-minute rundown of what’s happening on the internet.

items.name: Malicious Life
items.description: The history of cybersecurity, told through its biggest stories.

items.name: SANS Internet Storm Center
items.description: Daily handler diaries on what’s happening across the internet.

items.name: Krebs on Security
items.description: In-depth investigative reporting on cybercrime.

items.name: BleepingComputer
items.description: Fast, reliable security and technology news.

items.name: The DFIR Report
items.description: Real intrusions written up step by step, mapped to ATT&CK. Superb for learning how attacks unfold.

items.name: CISA cybersecurity advisories
items.description: Official alerts and advisories on active threats and vulnerabilities.

items.name: abuse.ch
items.description: MalwareBazaar, URLhaus and ThreatFox: free, community-fed threat intelligence feeds.

items.name: Unit 42 threat research
items.description: Detailed research on threat actors, malware and campaigns.

items.name: Talos Intelligence blog
items.description: Threat research and a weekly newsletter from one of the largest intel teams.

items.name: tl;dr sec
items.description: A weekly newsletter rounding up the best security tools, talks and articles.

items.name: This Week in 4n6
items.description: Every week’s digital forensics news, tools and research in one post.

items.name: CyberHeaven Discord
items.description: Our own community: ask questions, share progress and meet other learners.

items.name: r/cybersecurity
items.description: News, discussion and career questions from a large professional community.

items.name: r/AskNetsec
items.description: A place to ask technical security questions and get answers from practitioners.

items.name: OWASP chapters
items.description: Free local meetups on application security, all around the world.

items.name: BSides events
items.description: Community-run security conferences, often free or very cheap, in cities worldwide.

items.name: DEF CON Groups
items.description: Local hacker meetups that carry the DEF CON spirit year-round.

items.name: Women in CyberSecurity (WiCyS)
items.description: A community supporting the recruitment, retention and advancement of women in cybersecurity.

items.name: CyberSeek career pathway
items.description: An interactive map of cybersecurity roles, how they connect and what each requires.

items.name: NICE Workforce Framework
items.description: The standard breakdown of cybersecurity work roles, tasks and skills.
